newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault cuts prices to regain market share.
newsitem.headline: Renault cuts prices to regain market share.

text.p: Carmaker Renault SA said on Wednesday that it would cut car prices in France by up to five percent on some models to recapture lost market share.
It said it would simplify its price range, lower prices for some cars and offer more options without charging extra on others.

"The supplementary sales volumes generated by this ambitious new marketing policy will generate economies of scale to reinforce the cost-reduction programme announced in March," the company said in a statement.
It said the policy also aimed to reduce the gap between sticker prices and actual prices, which have been slashed in France by a fierce price war.
Beginning on October 1, prices for Clio, Megane, Laguna and Safrane models will be cut on average between 3.5 and five percent, it said.
The policy follows decisions by the group to leave prices unchanged at the start of the 1997 model year and to introduce Clio and Safrane models priced lower than their predecessors.
Renault's share of the French car market has fallen to 26 percent in the first half of 1996 from 33 percent at the start of 1995.
